reason: The text is a historical narrative describing the fall of Jerusalem under King Zedekiah's reign, the Babylonian siege, and the subsequent exile. While the passage contains descriptions of violence and destruction, it explicitly presents Zedekiah as doing "evil in the sight of the Lord" (וַיַּעַשׂ הָרַע בְּעֵינֵי יְהוָה), not as a model to emulate. The text portrays the catastrophic consequences of his poor leadership decisions (rebellion against Babylon), including the destruction of the Temple, the exile of the people, and his own capture and blinding. The narrative is descriptive and historically consequential, not prescriptive of violence as a leadership model. There is no statement in the text endorsing violence as exemplary or proper governance.
